title: tools/clean_test_db.py's run_psql() silently swallows FK-violation and other real failures whose stderr happens to contain "relation"
summary: Discovered while running the Step 00a Green-Main Gate for WF02-batch-0-20260811 (DDL-05, MIG-01, MIG-02, MIG-03). `zig build test-env-verify` reported C4 (schema baseline) FAIL: 11 leaked `public.tenant` rows (storage_mode='SCHEMA') with no matching `public.tenant_schemas` row or real Postgres schema -- left behind by an unrelated interrupted test run. `python tools/clean_test_db.py --include-fixtures` (the documented remedy, matching the exact ISS-0140/GH-443 half-provisioned-row scenario the script's own comments describe) reported 'Test database cleaned' with no errors, but the leaked rows were still present afterward -- reproduced identically both via the Bash tool's psql resolution and via PowerShell, ruling out the known Windows psql-shim resolution bug (GH-280/ISS-0040) as the cause.

root_cause.details: tools/clean_test_db.py run_psql() lines 102-116. The function runs psql as a subprocess and checks for non-zero exit at line 106 (`if result.returncode != 0:`). At line 109 it lowercases stderr (`stderr_lower = result.stderr.lower()`). Line 110-111 is the over-broad guard: `if "does not exist" in stderr_lower or "relation" in stderr_lower: return True`. This swallows any psql failure whose stderr contains either substring and returns True (success) with no warning printed. The intent (per the inline comment on line 109) was to ignore 'relation does not exist' when a table hasn't been created yet -- a valid no-op case. The defect: PostgreSQL FK-violation messages always contain 'relation' (e.g. 'ERROR:  insert or update on table "X" violates foreign key constraint "Y" ... referenced from relation "Z"'), so genuine DELETE failures caused by FK ordering, RLS, or any constraint error whose text references a relation name are silently classified as ignorable. Confirmed correct fix: (a) replace the unanchored substring check with either a SQLSTATE-based check (pass `--variable ON_ERROR_STOP=1` and inspect psql's exit to get error class), or match only the narrow anchored pattern `'does not exist'` without the `or 'relation'` branch; (b) add a post-condition re-query after every cleanup sweep that counts remaining leaked rows and exits non-zero / prints loudly if the expected post-state is not achieved, so the script cannot report 'Test database cleaned' when rows remain.

resolution: Fixed in tools/clean_test_db.py: (1) Removed over-broad `or 'relation'` substring guard from run_psql() — FK-violation messages always contain 'relation', causing real DELETE failures to be silently classified as ignorable. Now only the narrow 'does not exist' pattern is treated as a benign no-op. (2) Added _psql_is_native() helper to detect Windows .cmd psql shims (which ignore SQL arguments and always run SELECT 1 instead of the supplied DELETE statement). _psql_base_cmd() falls back to docker-compose exec when a shim is detected. (3) Added post-condition re-queries after every cleanup sweep — if rows remain after the sweep, the script raises RuntimeError instead of printing 'Test database cleaned'. (4) Added verbose warning log on any genuinely-ignorable error so silent swallowing is distinguishable from acknowledged no-ops in the output.
verification: 10/10 test-env-verify + 1067/1067 unit + 14/14 integration tests pass on feature/WF03-GH700-20260812. clean_test_db.py now raises RuntimeError on FK-violation failures and correctly falls back to docker-compose exec on Windows.
prevention: Match psql failures by SQLSTATE / a narrow, anchored error-class check, never by an unanchored substring like 'relation' that overlaps with normal FK-violation error text.
When ignoring a specific expected error class (missing table before first migration), print what was ignored and why, so a genuine silent failure is distinguishable from an expected no-op in the log.

Add a post-condition check after the cleanup sweep (query for remaining leaked rows) so the script itself fails loudly if its cleanup did not converge, rather than reporting 'Test database cleaned' unconditionally.
